name: Battle of Myriokephalon
note: The accounts do not say which way the pass ran or on which side of it the Seljuks stood; the road runs left to right, the heights above it and a second Seljuk force behind the column are placed by the needs of the story. The exact site of the battle is disputed, and the ruined fortress is placed in the vicinity of the pass without a known position. The rear division's arrival at the camp is shown after the emperor's, as the accounts have it. Where the Byzantine wings stood once the emperor broke out is not stated and they are left where they were.

phases.title: The Byzantine column enters the pass
phases.text: The Byzantine divisions entered the pass in a long column, vanguard first and the rear division last. The Seljuks held the heights above it, perhaps not yet fully deployed.
phases.quote: The Byzantine army was divided into a number of divisions, which entered the pass in the following order

phases.title: The leading divisions clear the pass
phases.text: The vanguard and main division went through with few casualties. Their infantry climbed the slopes and forced the Seljuks back to higher ground, while the divisions behind did not take this precaution.
phases.quote: These divisions sent their infantry up onto the slopes to dislodge the Seljuk soldiers, who were forced to withdraw to higher ground.

phases.title: The Turks close the trap on the right wing
phases.text: With the first two divisions out of the pass and the rear about to enter, the Turks attacked from the heights. The right wing lost cohesion and broke, and its commander Baldwin was killed.
phases.quote: The Turkish attack, descending from the heights, fell especially heavily on the Byzantine right wing.

phases.title: The baggage and siege trains are shot down
phases.text: The Turks then concentrated their attacks on the baggage and siege trains. They shot down the draught animals and choked the road.
phases.quote: The Turks then concentrated their attacks on the baggage and siege trains, shooting down the draught animals and choking the roadway.

phases.title: The left wing is struck and Kantakouzenos falls
phases.text: The left wing also suffered significant casualties. One of its leaders, John Kantakouzenos, was killed while fighting alone against a band of Seljuk soldiers.
phases.quote: The left-wing division also suffered significant casualties and one of its leaders, John Kantakouzenos, was slain when fighting alone against a band of Seljuk soldiers.

phases.title: The rear is attacked and a dust-storm falls
phases.text: The remaining Byzantine troops panicked at the carnage ahead and as the Turks began to attack their rear. A blinding dust-storm fell, and Manuel sat down to await his fate.
phases.quote: The remaining Byzantine troops were panicked by the carnage in front of them and the realisation that the Turks had also begun to attack their rear.

phases.title: Manuel forms up and leaves the pass
phases.text: Roused by his officers, Manuel restored discipline and formed a defensive order. His troops pushed past the wrecked baggage and out of the pass to join the van and main divisions, who had built a fortified camp.
phases.quote: when formed up, they pushed their way past the wreck of the baggage and out of the pass.

phases.title: The rear division reaches the camp
phases.text: The rear division under Andronikos Kontostephanos arrived at the camp somewhat later than the emperor, having suffered few casualties.
phases.quote: The rear division, under Andronikos Kontostephanos, arrived at the camp somewhat later than the emperor, having suffered few casualties.

phases.title: The camp repulses attacks through the night
phases.text: Seljuk mounted archers attacked the camp again and again through the night, and the Byzantines repulsed them each time.
phases.quote: The night was spent in successfully repulsing further attacks by Seljuk mounted archers.

phases.title: The Turks circle the camp and two counterattacks follow
phases.text: The Turks circled the camp firing arrows, and Manuel ordered two counterattacks, but there was no renewal of a general action.
phases.quote: The following day, the Turks circled the camp firing arrows; Manuel ordered two counterattacks
